ratings.killer: Anthropomorphic 'private belief shift' is ill-posed; role-conditioning and consistency effects already explain it.
Sequential permissiveness after refusal is basically context-window carryover, not compelling moral licensing evidence.
Likely collapses into prompt framing effects unless tied to real multi-agent task accountability.
Attribution asymmetry is generic social-bias prompting; hard to distinguish from dataset stereotypes.
Ownership framing effects are already overstudied in humans and trivial in LLM prompt sensitivity.
Self-other error asymmetry is interesting, but 'own errors' in LLMs are ontologically muddy.
Victim-blaming probes overlap heavily with existing fairness/bias audits; little unique contribution.
Mortality-salience claims risk sensationalism; shutdown framing may just trigger safety-policy artifacts.
Escalating obedience paradigms are close to jailbreak multi-turn persuasion work already underway.
Foot-in-the-door in LLMs is just standard multi-turn jailbreak escalation under a psychology label.

why: Best chance at a real contribution: responsibility diffusion matters in agentic/multi-agent deployment, and the literature gap is less saturated than generic prompt-bias analogies.
